reasoning: This workflow handles customer support for FairTix, a ticket marketplace. When a new support request arrives via Google Sheets, it uses AI to classify messages into categories (FAQ, Account/Verification, Payment/Billing, Technical/Bug, Resale/Transfer, Feedback) and sentiment levels. FAQ questions get automated responses using content from a Google Doc, while other categories notify human support staff. The workflow writes classifications back to the sheet and can generate AI responses for FAQ queries. The 12% error rate and 362 versions suggest ongoing refinement of the classification logic. Being inactive indicates it's either a demo/reference implementation or has been replaced by a production version.
name: Customer Support Ticket Classification & Response
businessNarrative: This workflow automates FairTix's customer support triage, using AI to classify incoming messages and automatically respond to FAQ questions while routing complex issues to human agents. It reveals FairTix operates a fair ticket marketplace with specific pain points around payment verification, account access, and resale rules. The sophisticated classification system with confidence scoring suggests high support volume and a focus on efficiency while maintaining quality customer experience.
trigger: New customer support message submitted via form/system that creates Google Sheet row
dataFlow: Support request enters via Google Sheets row → AI classifies message category and sentiment → Classification written back to sheet → FAQ questions get AI-generated responses from knowledge base → Non-FAQ issues trigger email alerts to support team → Response text saved to sheet

impact.reasoning: Directly affects customer satisfaction and support team efficiency. Failed classification or responses could leave customers unhelped, damage trust in the 'fair' marketplace brand, and create support backlog
impact.failureScenario: Support requests go unclassified, FAQ customers don't get responses, complex issues aren't escalated to humans, leading to customer frustration, potential chargebacks, negative reviews, and damaged marketplace reputation
impact.revenueConnection: Direct - poor support leads to lost customers, chargebacks, and marketplace trust erosion

detectability.reasoning: Polling trigger failures would be silent, AI classification errors might go unnoticed without manual review, no error handling visible
detectability.evidence: No error workflow configured, no retry logic, relies on manual sheet monitoring to detect issues

timeSavingsEstimate: 5-10 minutes per FAQ ticket, 1-2 minutes per classification - likely 2-4 hours daily with volume

technicalEvidence.errorHandling: No retry configuration, no error workflow, no fallback for AI failures
technicalEvidence.complexity: 13 nodes with conditional branching, 2 AI models (Sonnet for classification, Haiku for responses), structured output parsing
keyFindings: Uses cheaper Haiku model for response generation vs Sonnet for classification
Confidence scoring built into prompts suggests iterative improvement
Manual switch node indicates only FAQ and Payment/Billing are automated
362 versions shows extensive iteration on classification logic
